title: How I Evaluate Technical Projects
summary: I've developed a framework for evaluating student technical projects based on system design, ML rigor, and real-world viability that I apply as a judge at technical expos.
mainPoint: The core idea is that strong technical projects balance three dimensions: architectural soundness, methodological rigor, and practical applicability. Most weak projects fail on one or more of these.

outline.intro: Why I needed a framework when judging at CEAS Expo 2026
outline.point1: System Design - Is the architecture scalable? Do they understand tradeoffs?
outline.point2: Rigor - Did they validate their approach? Are claims backed by evidence?
outline.point3: Real-world Viability - Could this actually work in production? Are edge cases considered?
outline.conclusion: Combining these dimensions reveals project quality beyond surface-level impressive demos

title: How I'm Running My Job Search Like a System
summary: Instead of randomly applying to jobs, I've built a structured system around daily applications, referral outreach, and cold emails to founders/recruiters.
mainPoint: The core idea is that job search is a numbers game with a process. By systematizing applications, networking, and follow-ups, I can increase signal and reduce noise in my search for Summer/Fall 2026 roles.
